title: Chest pain - possible heart attack
description: Pressure, squeezing or heavy pain in the chest, often spreading to the left arm, jaw or back, with sweating, nausea or breathlessness. Risk is higher with age, diabetes, smoking and high blood pressure.
red_flags: Pain lasting more than a few minutes
Pain spreading to arm, jaw or back
advice: Treat as an emergency. Call 108 / 112 or go to the Emergency Department now. Do not drive yourself. Sit down and rest while waiting.

title: Stroke warning signs (FAST)
description: FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency. Also sudden loss of vision, balance or sudden confusion.
red_flags: Any FAST sign, even if it goes away
advice: Emergency. Note the time the symptoms started and call 108 / 112 immediately. Treatment works best in the first few hours.

title: Asthma flare / shortness of breath
description: Wheezing, cough and breathlessness, often at night or after triggers such as dust, smoke or exercise. Reliever inhaler helps less than usual.
red_flags: Too breathless to speak full sentences
advice: Use the reliever inhaler as in the written asthma plan and sit upright. Be seen by a doctor within 1-2 hours; go to Emergency if breathing gets worse.

title: Migraine and tension-type headache
description: Recurring headache, one-sided and throbbing (migraine) or band-like (tension), sometimes with nausea or sensitivity to light. Similar to previous headaches.
red_flags: Headache with fever and stiff neck
advice: Rest in a dark quiet room, drink water. A pharmacist can advise on simple pain relief. Book a routine appointment if headaches are frequent.

title: Fever and flu-like illness in adults
description: Fever, body aches, tiredness, sore throat or runny nose for a few days. Usually a viral infection that gets better on its own within a week.
red_flags: Fever above 39.5 C for more than 3 days
advice: Rest, drink plenty of fluids. A pharmacist can advise on fever relief. See a doctor if fever lasts more than 3 days or warning signs appear.

title: Suspected dengue fever
description: High fever with severe body and joint pain, pain behind the eyes and sometimes a rash, often during the monsoon season. Needs a blood test.
red_flags: Severe stomach pain or repeated vomiting
advice: Get a same-day or next-day blood test at the OPD. Drink plenty of fluids. Avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless a doctor says so.

title: Gastroenteritis - vomiting and diarrhoea
description: Loose stools and/or vomiting, often after outside food or water, usually settling in 2-3 days. Main risk is dehydration.
red_flags: Unable to keep fluids down for 24 hours
advice: Sip oral rehydration solution (ORS) often. Eat light food when ready. See a doctor if it lasts more than 3 days or signs of dehydration appear.

title: Acute abdominal pain - possible appendicitis
description: Pain that starts around the navel and moves to the lower right abdomen, getting worse over hours, often with fever, nausea and loss of appetite.
red_flags: Severe pain that is getting worse
advice: Be seen by a doctor within 1-2 hours. Do not eat until examined. Go to Emergency if the pain becomes severe.

title: Sprain or minor limb injury
description: Pain and swelling after twisting a joint, able to put some weight on it. Most sprains heal in 2-6 weeks.
advice: RICE: Rest, Ice (20 minutes at a time), Compression and Elevation. Book an orthopaedics appointment if not improving in a week; same day if you cannot bear weight.

title: Skin rash and mild allergic reaction
description: Itchy red patches or raised hives, often after a new food, soap or medicine, without breathing problems or face swelling.
red_flags: Swelling of lips, tongue or throat
Rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass
advice: Avoid the suspected trigger. A pharmacist can advise on antihistamines. Book a dermatology appointment if it lasts more than a week.

title: Sore throat and ear pain
description: Painful throat or ear, often with a cold. Most cases are viral and settle within a week.
red_flags: Cannot swallow saliva or open the mouth
Discharge from the ear with high fever
advice: Warm salt-water gargles, fluids and rest. See ENT if not better in a week or if warning signs appear.

title: Fever in a child
description: Fever in a child, often with cold or cough. Most are mild viral illnesses, but young babies and drowsy children need quick review.
red_flags: Baby under 3 months with any fever
Very drowsy or hard to wake
Not drinking or no wet nappy for 12 hours
advice: Keep the child drinking fluids and lightly dressed. Book a same-day paediatrics visit; go to Emergency for any warning sign.

title: Low mood, anxiety and thoughts of self-harm
description: Feeling low, hopeless, anxious or stressed for weeks, poor sleep or appetite, losing interest in things.
red_flags: Thoughts of ending life or self-harm
advice: Talk to someone you trust. Book a counselling appointment. Tele-MANAS 14416 is free and 24x7. If you might act on thoughts of self-harm, go to Emergency now.

title: Diabetes - high or low blood sugar
description: Low sugar: shaking, sweating, confusion. High sugar: thirst, passing a lot of urine, tiredness, sometimes vomiting.
red_flags: Low sugar not improving after sugary drink
advice: If low: take a sugary drink or glucose now and recheck in 15 minutes. If high and unwell: be seen by a doctor within 1-2 hours.
